bib.title: ParamMem: Augmenting Language Agents with Parametric Reflective Memory

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ParamMem: Augmenting Language Agents with Parametric Reflective Memory", Tianjun Yao, Yongqiang Chen, Yujia Zheng, Pan Li, Zhiqiang Shen, Kun Zhang (MBZUAI, CMU, Georgia Tech). Preprint (header "Preprint. March 2, 2026"; arXiv 2602.23320v2, 27 Feb 2026, cs.LG). First author month/year: Yao, Feb 2026. No venue.

COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages, 78,230 chars read (body, tables, appendices A and B, prompt figures). The references were skimmed only.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Reflective diversity correlates with task success under Reflexion, DoT and DoT-bank.
  number: avg Pearson r = 0.76 (per dataset: 2WikiMQA 0.95, HotpotQA 0.97, MATH 0.91, HumanEval 0.75, MBPP 0.22)
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B, 5 datasets, diversity = mean pairwise cosine distance across multi-round reflections per sample. This is correlation across three methods, not a causal test.
  quote: "the average Pearson correlation coefficient across the five datasets is 0.76, indicating a strong positive relationship between reflective diversity and task performance."
  where: p1, Fig 1
- ParamMem is a LoRA-tuned small LM that generates reflections from learned cross-sample patterns, in place of retrieval. It beats Reflexion, DoT, DoT-bank and Retroformer on code and QA.
  number: HumanEval Llama-3.1-8B: Base 59.15, Reflexion 76.22, DoT-bank 79.56, ParamAgent 82.93. Mistral-7B: 32.93 base, DoT-bank 54.26, ParamAgent 67.07. HotpotQA Llama: ParamAgent 78.33 vs Reflexion 71.33. 2Wiki Llama: 88.67 vs DoT-bank 80.33.
  setup: Table 1, 5 iterations, three backbones (Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Qwen2-1.5B). Evaluation sets are small: HumanEval 164, MBPP 397, MATH 278, HotpotQA and 2Wiki 300 each. Single runs, no variance reported.
  quote: "ParamAgent 82.93↑23.78" (HumanEval, Llama-3.1-8B); "Reflexion 76.22↑17.07"
  where: p6, Table 1
- On MATH, the cross-sample bank matters more than ParamMem alone, and Retroformer is better there.
  number: MATH Llama: DoT-bank 73.02, ParamAgent 67.99, ParamAgent-plus 75.45, Retroformer 63.67
  quote: "ParamAgent-plus 75.45↑27.25"
  where: p6, Table 1 and Obs 1
- Fine-tuning raises reflection diversity. This holds even when the model is tuned on its own outputs.
  number: mean pairwise cosine distance 0.351 (tuned on GPT-4o-mini data), 0.256 (tuned on Llama-3.1-8B's own data), 0.200 (frozen). Optimal K-means clusters: ParamAgent 39 vs Reflexion 11, DoT 32, DoT-bank 33. Silhouette 0.240 vs 0.061 / 0.171 / 0.173.
  setup: HumanEval, 10 reflections per task at T=1.0, text-embedding-3-small embeddings
  quote: "GPT-4o-mini (avg: 0.351) Llama3.1-8B (avg: 0.256) Frozen (avg: 0.200)"
  where: p7, Fig 4
- Self-improvement without a stronger teacher: ParamMem trained on Llama-3.1-8B's own synthetic data still helps.
  number: HumanEval 78.05 (ParamAgent), 86.59 (ParamAgent-plus) vs DoT-bank 79.56; HotpotQA 76.33 and 83.33 vs DoT-bank 72.00
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B is both agent and data generator (Table 2). Note: on HumanEval, ParamAgent (self-data) 78.05 is below DoT-bank 79.56. The "significantly improves over DoT-bank" claim is clear only for ParamAgent-plus and for HotpotQA.
  quote: "ParamAgent-plus 86.59↑27.44 83.33↑25.66"
  where: p6, Table 2
- Iterative self-teaching gives steady gains for ParamAgent, with no correctness filtering.
  number: HumanEval Pass@1 78.66, 81.71, 82.93 over iterations 1-3 (ParamAgent). ParamAgent-plus 87.20, 87.80, 87.80 (marginal).
  setup: 1,000 examples, 3 rounds of regenerating targets from the model's own outputs and refitting, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, HumanEval only
  quote: "Our approach requires no filtering, since ParamMem targets diversity rather than correctness."
  where: p7, Fig 5, Obs 5
- Weak-to-strong: an 8B or 30B ParamMem helps an 80B agent.
  number: Qwen3-Next-80B agent. LiveCodeBench: Simple 52.00, Reflexion 62.00, ParamAgent-plus (Qwen3-30B ParamMem) 68.00. HumanEval 90.24 -> 98.17. HotpotQA with Llama-8B ParamMem: ParamAgent-plus 85.00 vs DoT-bank 83.33.
  quote: "ParamAgent-plus 63.33↑11.33 98.17↑7.93 85.00↑13.67" (Llama-3.1-8B ParamMem row)
  where: p7, Table 3. Also Appendix Tables 6 and 7, p14-15: Llama-3.1-70B HumanEval ParamAgent-plus 95.03 vs DoT-bank 92.68; HotpotQA 89.67 vs 80.00 (Reflexion 82.33).
  caveat: some gaps are small, e.g. HotpotQA ParamAgent 79.67 on Qwen3-80B ties DoT. The "9.7%" and "2.0%" figures in the text are relative gains.
- Sample efficiency: 500 K-means-selected samples nearly match 8,000.
  number: HumanEval 81.71 (500) vs 82.93 (8000); MBPP 64.99 vs 67.00; ParamAgent-plus (500) 86.59 / 65.49
  setup: GPT-4o-mini synthetic data, Llama-3.1-8B, LoRA
  quote: "ParamAgent(500 samples) 81.71 64.99"
  where: p8, Table 4
- Cost: more tokens. ParamAgent uses roughly 10 to 24 times the Base prompt tokens in places, and it is the authors' only conceded limitation.
  number: HotpotQA Llama-8B prompt tokens 3,649,598 (ParamAgent) vs 703,192 (Reflexion) vs 2,179,148 (DoT-bank); cost $0.680 vs $0.139 vs $0.427 (Table 8). HumanEval ParamAgent $0.17603 vs Reflexion $0.07589.
  setup: TogetherAI pricing, Aug 20 2025, $0.18 per million tokens
  quote: "A notable one is the increased token consumption in certain scenarios, which is an inherent cost of the additional reflective diversity."
  where: p9 (Limitations), p15 (Table 8)
- Mechanics: the module is trained on GPT-4o-mini-generated reflection data, not on the agent's real failures.
  number: LoRA rank 128, alpha 32, lr 2e-5, 3 epochs. Data: 4,000 APPS problems + 4,200 synthetic for code; 800 MATH problems per subject; 10,000 per QA set. At inference, T=0.2 on iteration 1 and T=1.0 after; 5 iterations.
  quote: "the parametric model is instantiated using Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, and is finetuned via LoRA. For LoRA finetuning, we use a rank of r= 128 , scaling factor α= 32, a learning rate of 2e−5 , and train for 3 epochs."
  where: p5; Appendix B.2, p13-14

LIMITS
- Authors concede only token cost.
- ParamMem is trained offline on synthetic reflection data ("global-level reflection" = a list of likely mistakes, or a query decomposition). It does not learn from the agent's own episodes and does not interact with the environment at inference ("ParamMem does not directly interact with the environment").
- This is not lesson-learning from failure. The contribution is diversity of hints.
- Causality from diversity to accuracy is argued by correlation (MBPP r = 0.22) and one case study.
- No variance or seeds. Small test sets. Mostly small open models plus a few 70-80B runs.
- Most self-improvement evidence is HumanEval and HotpotQA. Iterative self-teaching is HumanEval only.
- No comparison against simply sampling reflections more times from the frozen model at high temperature, or against equal-token budgets. The frozen model's diversity is 0.200 vs 0.256.
- No test of forgetting, drift or update cost over a long-running deployment.
- Retroformer wins on MATH.
- Prose says "consistent" gains. MBPP Mistral DoT-bank (24.68) is below Base (24.94), and ParamAgent-plus is missing from several Table 1 rows.

BUILDS ON: Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); DoT / DoT-bank (Lingam et al., 2025), whose retrieval it reuses; Retroformer (Yao et al., 2023c); LoRA (Hu et al., 2022); STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022) and ReST/ReST-EM, SPIN, Self-Rewarding LMs for self-improvement; ExpeL (Zhao et al., 2024), Self-RAG, LEMA, SCoRe, MemoryLLM, MemGPT, Generative Agents and MemoryBank as related memory work (Appendix A); Self-Refine (Madaan 2023), least-to-most prompting (Zhou 2022).

CODE: Algorithm 1 (p4) is the loop. For each task x, up to Tmax iterations: sample rg_t from Mg at T=0.2 on the first iteration and 1.0 after. Retrieve episodic reflections r_1:t-1 and have the actor generate y_t conditioned on x, r_1:t-1 and rg_t. If EVALUATE passes, store the trajectory in bank B and break. Otherwise generate a self-reflection into M. Phase 2 (ParamAgent-plus) re-attempts failed tasks with RETRIEVESIMILAR(B, x, j) trajectories added. Eq. 4: y_k ~ p_θ(· | x, r_1:k-1, RETRIEVE(B,x), rg_k).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): scatter of diversity vs accuracy across 5 datasets. It motivates the whole paper.
- Fig 2 (p3): the memory comparison diagram, with episodic only, plus cross-sample, plus parametric. It shows the three media in one picture.
- Fig 3 (p4): sample ParamMem outputs.
- Fig 4 (p7): diversity histograms and clusters.
- Fig 5 (p7): 3-round self-teaching curve.
- Fig 8 (p17): side-by-side reflections from Reflexion, DoT and ParamAgent on one MBPP problem. It is the clearest intuition for what "diverse" means.
- Figs 9-11 (p18-19): the 1-shot training-data construction prompts.

FIT TO TARGET NOTE: It is a usable but narrow citation for note 08's "parameters" medium. It shows reflections stored in weights (a LoRA module) as a complement to episodic and retrieved memory. It also shows that self-generated data helps, and that the module can be small and transfer to a stronger agent. Do not use it as evidence that lessons from the agent's own failures are learned into weights. The training data is synthetic, offline and independent of the agent's trajectories, and the target is diversity. Use as an example of a parametric medium with a cost and a diminishing-returns caveat (ParamAgent-plus gains little from self-teaching). Note 05 (long-running loop memory) fits less well, since the paper has no long-horizon or persistent-state results. It belongs with note 08 or a memory/reflection note. Contrast with experience docs: the retrieval-based DoT-bank and ParamAgent-plus combine both.

PROBLEMS: None serious. No embedded instructions. Table text extraction is run together in places (e.g. "82.93↑23.7819.18" is score 82.93, delta 23.78, tokens 19.18). The Table 3 row labels for the two ParamMem instantiations were lost as icons, so which row is which was inferred from the text (first pair = Llama-3.1-8B, second pair = Qwen3-30B). Table 1 has no ParamAgent-plus rows except MATH. Table 8 cost for ParamAgent on HumanEval is garbled with the Pass@1 column.
